records.name: DELIVER
records.q: Dapagliflozin vs placebo, HF with EF >40%
records.res: ↓ worsening HF/CV death, HR 0.82
records.why: Completes SGLT2i benefit across the full LVEF spectrum
records.gl: POSTDATES the Apr-2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline (DELIVER published Sep 2022). Supports current practice; NOT evidence incorporated into that guideline.
records.note: CORRECTED per Codex: originally claimed 'incorporated into 2022 guideline' — chronologically impossible.

records.name: EAST-AFNET 4
records.q: Early rhythm control vs usual care, AF ≤1yr
records.res: ↓ composite HR 0.79; stopped early
records.why: Overturns AFFIRM-era teaching that rhythm control offers no outcome advantage

records.name: CASTLE-AF
records.q: Ablation vs medical therapy, AF + HFrEF
records.res: ↓ death/HF hosp HR 0.62
records.why: Ablation as disease-modifying, not just symptom control, in AF+HFrEF

records.name: COAPT
records.q: TEER + GDMT vs GDMT, secondary MR
records.res: ↓ HF hosp 35.8 vs 67.9%/pt-yr; ↓ mortality 29.1 vs 46.1%
records.why: Defines who benefits, in contrast to the negative MITRA-FR

records.name: CLEAR Outcomes
records.q: Bempedoic acid vs placebo, statin-intolerant
records.res: ↓ MACE HR 0.87
records.why: First outcomes evidence for a non-statin agent in statin intolerance
records.gl: incorporated into the 2026 dyslipidemia guideline. The 2022 ACC nonstatin pathway described CLEAR Outcomes as still ONGOING.
records.note: CORRECTED per Codex: guideline relationship fixed (2026 dyslipidemia guideline; the 2022 ACC pathway described the trial as ONGOING). Metadata RESOLVED 2026-07-17: NEJM 2023;388:1353-64, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2215024, double-blind RCT.

records.name: COLCOT
records.q: Colchicine 0.5mg post-MI
records.res: ↓ composite HR 0.77
records.why: First large RCT showing anti-inflammatory therapy cuts recurrent CV events

records.name: STICH
records.q: CABG + medical vs medical alone, EF ≤35%
records.res: Primary: no mortality benefit at 5y (HR 0.86, p=0.12)
records.why: Classic case of reading a trial rather than a headline
records.note: Paired with STICHES per Jenni's decision. THIS record is the 2011 NEUTRAL primary endpoint. Do not teach the positive 10-year result off this PMID.

records.name: AFFIRM-AHF
records.q: IV ferric carboxymaltose post-acute HF
records.res: ↓ HF hosp RR 0.74; primary composite p=0.059
records.why: Screen ferritin/TSAT at HF discharge; oral iron is not a substitute
records.note: Metadata RESOLVED 2026-07-17: Lancet 2020;396(10266):1895-1904, RCT; PubMed record confirmed directly.

records.name: LoDoCo2
records.q: Colchicine in chronic coronary disease
records.res: ↓ composite HR 0.69
records.why: Extends the anti-inflammatory benefit to stable CAD

records.name: NOTT
records.q: Continuous vs nocturnal O2, hypoxemic COPD
records.res: Nocturnal-only mortality 1.94x continuous
records.why: Mortality benefit requires CONTINUOUS use — drives adherence counselling

records.name: IMPACT
records.q: Single-inhaler triple vs dual, COPD
records.res: ↓ exac 15% vs ICS-LABA, 25% vs LAMA-LABA; ↑ pneumonia
records.why: When to step up to triple therapy, and the pneumonia trade-off

records.name: ETHOS
records.q: BGF triple at two ICS doses
records.res: ↓ exac 24% vs LAMA-LABA; ↑ pneumonia
records.why: Confirmatory companion to IMPACT

records.name: PEITHO
records.q: Tenecteplase in intermediate-risk PE
records.res: ↓ death/decompensation 2.6 vs 5.6% BUT major bleed 6.3 vs 1.2%, hemorrhagic stroke 2.0 vs 0.2%
records.why: Why we do NOT routinely lyse intermediate-risk PE
records.gl: guidelines have NOT adopted routine lysis (ACCP/ESC)

records.name: MIST2
records.q: Intrapleural tPA+DNase, pleural infection
records.res: ↓ surgical referral 4 vs 16%; single agents ineffective
records.why: Combination, not monotherapy — bedside empyema management

records.name: ACURASYS
records.q: Cisatracurium 48h in severe ARDS
records.res: 90-day mortality HR 0.68 — POSITIVE
records.why: Positive in 2010, then ROSE (2019) failed to reproduce it. The reversal IS the lesson.
records.gl: conditional recommendation only, reflecting the ACURASYS/ROSE conflict
records.note: CORRECTED per Codex: was mislabeled 'important negative trial'. ACURASYS was POSITIVE; ROSE contradicted it.

records.name: DEXA-ARDS
records.q: Dexamethasone in moderate-severe ARDS
records.res: +4.8 ventilator-free days; 60-d mortality 21 vs 36%
records.why: Pre-COVID steroid anchor in ARDS, distinct from RECOVERY

records.name: AMPLIFY
records.q: Apixaban monotherapy vs enox/warfarin, acute VTE
records.res: Noninferior; major bleed 0.6 vs 1.8%
records.why: Basis for apixaban-only VTE regimens with no heparin lead-in

records.name: CARAVAGGIO
records.q: Apixaban vs dalteparin, cancer VTE
records.res: Noninferior; NO excess GI bleeding
records.why: The cancer-VTE DOAC without the GI bleeding penalty

records.name: TRICC
records.q: Restrictive (7) vs liberal (10) transfusion, ICU
records.res: In-hospital mortality 22.3 vs 28.1%
records.why: Foundational restrictive-transfusion trial

records.name: REALITY
records.q: Restrictive vs liberal transfusion in MI
records.res: MACE 11.0 vs 14.0%, noninferior but CI does not exclude harm
records.why: TRICC excluded ACS; REALITY tries to fill the gap and does not fully settle it

records.name: TRAPS
records.q: Rivaroxaban vs warfarin, triple-positive APS
records.res: STOPPED EARLY: thrombotic events 12% vs 0%
records.why: The best 'DOACs are not interchangeable' case in medicine

records.name: HOKUSAI-VTE Cancer
records.q: Edoxaban vs dalteparin, cancer VTE
records.res: Noninferior; ↑ major bleeding 6.9 vs 4.0%, GI-driven
records.why: The bleeding trade-off in luminal GI cancer

records.name: SELECT-D
records.q: Rivaroxaban vs dalteparin, cancer VTE
records.res: ↓ recurrence 4 vs 11%; ↑ CRNM bleed 13 vs 4%
records.why: Signalled the GI/GU bleeding risk that shaped guideline caution

records.name: WAKE-UP
records.q: Alteplase by DWI-FLAIR mismatch, unknown onset
records.why: Imaging can substitute for the clock in wake-up stroke

records.name: EXTEND
records.q: Alteplase 4.5-9h by perfusion imaging
records.why: Extends the window, at a real sICH cost

records.name: AcT
records.q: Tenecteplase vs alteplase
records.res: Noninferior; similar sICH
records.why: Single bolus simplifies transfer for thrombectomy
records.gl: incorporated into the CURRENT 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline
records.note: CORRECTED per Codex: previously cited a vague '2023 update'.

records.name: CHANCE
records.q: Clopidogrel+ASA, minor stroke/TIA (China)
records.res: ↓ stroke 8.2 vs 11.7%; NO excess bleeding
records.why: Half of the single best generalizability lesson in the batch

records.name: POINT
records.q: Clopidogrel+ASA, international
records.res: ↓ composite 5.0 vs 6.5%; major hemorrhage 0.9 vs 0.4%
records.why: The other half: same intervention, different population, real bleeding cost

records.name: THALES
records.q: Ticagrelor+ASA, minor stroke/TIA
records.res: ↓ stroke/death 5.5 vs 6.6%; severe bleed HR 3.99; no disability-free gain
records.why: Why ticagrelor did not displace clopidogrel

records.name: WATERFALL
records.q: Aggressive vs moderate fluids, acute pancreatitis
records.res: STOPPED EARLY FOR HARM: fluid overload 20.5 vs 6.3%, no efficacy gain
records.why: Directly refutes dogma residents are still taught

records.name: SONIC
records.q: Infliximab +/- azathioprine, Crohn
records.res: Steroid-free remission 56.8 / 44.4 / 30.0%
records.why: Basis for combination biologic strategy

records.name: CALM
records.q: Treat-to-target vs symptom-driven, Crohn
records.res: Mucosal healing 45.9 vs 30.3%
records.why: Biomarker-driven escalation beats symptom-driven
records.gl: underpins STRIDE-II (which is a CONSENSUS doc, not an RCT)

records.name: CONFIRM
records.q: Terlipressin + albumin vs placebo + albumin, HRS-1
records.res: ↑ HRS reversal, BUT significant RESPIRATORY FAILURE harm signal
records.why: The efficacy/respiratory-failure trade-off that governs terlipressin use
records.gl: informs AASLD guidance and the FDA label's respiratory warning
records.note: REPLACES an incorrect entry. The prior draft substituted a 1995 octreotide/sclerotherapy variceal-bleeding study — a different clinical question entirely. Caught by Codex.

records.name: REPRIEVE
records.q: Pitavastatin in HIV below statin threshold
records.res: ↓ MACE HR 0.65; stopped early
records.why: HIV is an independent CV risk factor not captured by ASCVD calculators

records.name: Study 31 / A5349
records.q: 4-month rifapentine-moxi vs 6-month TB regimen
records.res: Noninferior; the non-moxifloxacin arm FAILED noninferiority
records.why: Shorter TB therapy improves completion

records.name: BALANCE (bacteremia)
records.q: 7 vs 14 days antibiotics for bloodstream infection
records.res: 90-day mortality 14.5 vs 16.1%; noninferior
records.why: Largest, most generalizable short-course bacteremia trial (3,608 pts)
records.gl: incorporated (IDSA 2025 duration guidance). NOTE S. aureus was EXCLUDED.
records.note: DISAMBIGUATION: a different trial named BALANCE tests lithium+valproate in bipolar disorder. This is the bacteremia one.

records.name: OVIVA
records.q: Oral vs IV antibiotics, bone and joint infection
records.res: Failure 13.2% oral vs 14.6% IV; noninferior; shorter LOS
records.why: Overturns the 'IV required' dogma for bone/joint infection

records.name: STOP-IT
records.q: Fixed ~4d vs physiology-guided antibiotics after source control, cIAI
records.res: Composite 21.8 vs 22.3%, no difference despite 4 vs 8 days
records.why: Stop on a fixed timeline; do not chase fever/leukocytosis

records.name: MERINO
records.q: Pip-tazo vs meropenem, ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli/Klebsiella bacteremia
records.res: 30-day mortality 12.3 vs 3.7% — pip-tazo FAILED noninferiority
records.why: Do not use pip-tazo for ESBL bacteremia even if susceptible in vitro

records.name: SABATO
records.q: Early oral switch in LOW-RISK S. aureus bacteremia
records.res: Noninferior, but stopped early at 215/430 for slow recruitment
records.why: Strict low-risk criteria must be applied before extrapolating
records.note: Underpowered due to early stopping — flag when teaching.

records.name: DOTS
records.q: Dalbavancin (2 doses) vs standard IV therapy, complicated S. aureus bacteremia
records.res: DOOR 47.7% — did NOT meet superiority; noninferior on efficacy
records.why: Line-avoidance strategy after cultures clear
records.gl: too recent for the 2026 IDSA/ESCMID SAB guidance
records.note: NAMING CAVEAT: DOTS tests IV dalbavancin, NOT 'partial oral therapy' as the queue described. Confirm this is the intended trial.
records.pubtype_override_reason: JAMA 2025 — title states 'The DOTS Randomized Clinical Trial'; PubMed indexed only as Journal Article

records.name: SAFE
records.q: Albumin vs saline, ICU resuscitation
records.res: No mortality difference (RR 0.99); later TBI subgroup harm signal
records.why: Crystalloid remains default; avoid albumin in TBI

records.name: FACTT
records.q: Conservative vs liberal fluids in ARDS
records.res: No mortality difference; +2.5 ventilator-free days, +2.2 ICU-free days
records.why: 'Dry lungs' after resuscitation — shortens vent and ICU time

records.name: CLOVERS
records.q: Early restrictive fluids/earlier pressors vs liberal, sepsis-induced hypotension
records.res: STOPPED FOR FUTILITY: 14.0 vs 14.9%, p=0.61
records.why: Genuine equipoise — judgement beats protocol
records.gl: SSC has not resolved this; CLOVERS reinforces equipoise

records.name: CLASSIC
records.q: Restricted vs standard IV fluid, established septic shock
records.res: 90-day mortality 42.3 vs 42.1% despite 1798 vs 3811 mL
records.why: 'Less fluid' is safe but not superior
records.gl: not yet in a formal updated recommendation

records.name: TRISS
records.q: Transfusion threshold 7 vs 9 g/dL, septic shock
records.res: 90-day mortality 43 vs 45%; half the units
records.why: Restrictive threshold safe in septic shock

records.name: MIND-USA
records.q: Haloperidol/ziprasidone vs placebo, ICU delirium
records.res: NO difference in days alive without delirium/coma
records.why: Do not reflexively give antipsychotics for ICU delirium
records.gl: incorporated (SCCM PADIS: recommends against routine use)

records.name: RALES
records.q: Spironolactone in NYHA III-IV HFrEF
records.res: Mortality 35 vs 46%, RR 0.70; stopped early
records.why: MRA as a GDMT pillar; prototype for K+/renal monitoring

records.name: EPHESUS
records.q: Eplerenone post-MI with EF ≤40%
records.res: Mortality 14.4 vs 16.7%, RR 0.85; ↑ serious hyperkalemia
records.why: Extends MRA benefit to post-MI; benefit vs hyperkalemia trade-off

records.name: COMPLETE
records.q: Complete vs culprit-only revascularization after STEMI
records.res: CV death/MI 7.8 vs 10.5%, HR 0.74
records.why: Routine staged non-culprit PCI after STEMI

records.name: FAME
records.q: FFR-guided vs angiography-guided PCI, multivessel
records.res: 1-yr composite 13.2 vs 18.3%, p=0.02
records.why: Physiology beats anatomy for lesion selection
records.note: FAME 2 (PMID 22924638) is a DISTINCT trial: FFR-guided PCI vs medical therapy. Do not conflate.

records.name: FREEDOM
records.q: CABG vs PCI in diabetes with multivessel CAD
records.res: 5-yr composite 18.7 vs 26.6% favouring CABG; stroke higher with CABG 5.2 vs 2.4%
records.why: CABG preferred in diabetic multivessel disease; composite trade-off teaching

records.name: AUGUSTUS
records.q: 2x2: apixaban vs VKA, aspirin vs placebo, AF after ACS/PCI
records.res: Apixaban less bleeding HR 0.69; aspirin MORE bleeding HR 1.89 without ischemic benefit
records.why: Defines the modern default: DOAC + P2Y12, drop aspirin early

records.name: INVICTUS
records.q: Rivaroxaban vs VKA in rheumatic heart disease AF
records.res: Rivaroxaban WORSE (HR ~1.7 favouring VKA)
records.why: Critical exception to DOAC-over-warfarin: rheumatic MS still needs warfarin

records.name: TORCH
records.q: Salmeterol/fluticasone vs placebo, COPD mortality
records.res: Mortality 12.6 vs 15.2%, p=0.052 — narrowly MISSED
records.why: Classic 'just missed significance' teaching case

records.name: FLAME
records.q: LABA/LAMA vs LABA/ICS, COPD
records.res: LABA/LAMA superior, RR 0.88; fewer pneumonias 3.2 vs 4.8%
records.why: Shifted first-line away from routine ICS

records.name: LOTT
records.q: Long-term O2 for MODERATE desaturation (SpO2 89-93%)
records.res: No benefit (HR 0.94)
records.why: Do NOT prescribe home O2 for SpO2 89-93% — NOTT does not extrapolate

records.name: HOT-HMV
records.q: Home NIV + O2 vs O2 alone after hypercapnic COPD exacerbation
records.res: Median time to readmission/death 4.3 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.49
records.why: Discharge planning for persistent hypercapnia

records.name: SAMMPRIS
records.q: Aggressive medical therapy vs intracranial stenting
records.res: 30-day stroke/death 14.7 vs 5.8% — stenting HARMFUL; stopped early
records.why: Medical management beats stenting for intracranial atherosclerosis

records.name: NASCET
records.q: CEA vs medical therapy, symptomatic ≥70% carotid stenosis
records.res: ARR 17 percentage points at 2 years; stopped early
records.why: Foundational carotid revascularization trial

records.name: SPS3 (antiplatelet)
records.q: Clopidogrel+ASA vs ASA, recent lacunar stroke
records.res: No stroke reduction; major hemorrhage nearly DOUBLED, ↑ mortality
records.why: Long-term DAPT harms in small-vessel stroke
records.note: SPS3 had a SECOND randomization (BP target), reported separately: Lancet 2013, PMID 23726159. Keep distinct.

records.name: NAVIGATE ESUS
records.q: Rivaroxaban vs aspirin after embolic stroke of undetermined source
records.res: No stroke reduction; major bleeding HR 2.72; stopped early
records.why: Refutes empiric anticoagulation for ESUS
records.note: PMID CORRECTED (Codex + verified): was 30188630 = correspondence [Letter, Comment]. Canonical primary results = Hart RG et al, NEJM 2018;378:2191-2201, PMID 29766772, n=7213, stopped early for lack of efficacy + harm.

records.name: SORT (albumin in SBP)
records.q: Albumin + cefotaxime vs cefotaxime alone, SBP
records.res: Renal impairment 10 vs 33%; in-hospital mortality 10 vs 29%
records.why: The albumin order set residents write in SBP

records.name: STOPAH
records.q: Prednisolone and/or pentoxifylline, severe alcohol-associated hepatitis
records.res: Prednisolone OR 0.61 at 28d (p=0.06), gone by 90d; pentoxifylline no benefit
records.why: Steroid signal is marginal and does not persist; pentoxifylline has no role

records.name: ATTIRE
records.q: Targeted albumin infusions, hospitalized decompensated cirrhosis
records.res: No benefit; MORE serious adverse events incl. pulmonary edema
records.why: Counters the 'more albumin is better' reflex
records.gl: incorporated (AASLD/EASL restrict albumin to specific indications)

records.name: HALT-IT
records.q: Tranexamic acid in acute GI bleeding
records.res: No mortality benefit; ↑ VTE and seizures
records.why: Do not extrapolate CRASH-2 trauma data to GI bleeding

records.name: DPP
records.q: Lifestyle vs metformin vs placebo in impaired glucose tolerance
records.res: Diabetes incidence ↓58% lifestyle, ↓31% metformin
records.why: Prediabetes is modifiable; lifestyle beats metformin

records.name: WHI (E+P)
records.q: Estrogen+progestin vs placebo, healthy postmenopausal women
records.res: Stopped early: ↑ CHD (HR 1.29), ↑ invasive breast cancer, ↑ stroke/VTE
records.why: Why MHT prescribing collapsed after 2002
records.gl: incorporated (USPSTF recommends against for chronic disease prevention)

records.name: HERS
records.q: Estrogen+progestin for SECONDARY prevention of CHD
records.res: No overall benefit (RH 0.99); early harm in year 1
records.why: With WHI, why HT is never started for cardioprotection
records.gl: predates but is foundational to current guidance

records.name: CATIE
records.q: Four SGAs vs perphenazine, chronic schizophrenia
records.res: 74% discontinued by 18 months; olanzapine longest but worst metabolic
records.why: Reframes selection around side-effect profile, not drug generation

records.name: STICHES
records.q: STICH Extension Study: CABG + medical therapy vs medical therapy alone, ischemic cardiomyopathy, 10-year follow-up
records.res: 10-year all-cause mortality 58.9% vs 66.1%, p=0.02 — POSITIVE at 10 years
records.why: The other half of the STICH story: a neutral 5-year primary endpoint that became significant with longer follow-up. Teach the pair, never one alone.
records.gl: incorporated (2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI, Class I for CABG in ischemic cardiomyopathy)
records.note: LINKED to STICH (PMID 21463150). Per Jenni's decision: keep both, clearly separated.

records.name: ProCESS
records.q: Protocol-based EGDT vs protocol-based standard vs usual care, early septic shock
records.res: 60-day mortality 21.0 / 18.2 / 18.9% — no difference
records.why: First of the triad refuting Rivers EGDT

records.name: ARISE
records.q: EGDT vs usual care, early septic shock (Australasia)
records.res: 90-day mortality 18.6 vs 18.8%
records.why: Largest of the triad; reproduced ProCESS in another health system

records.name: ProMISe
records.q: EGDT vs usual care, septic shock (UK NHS)
records.res: 90-day mortality 29.5 vs 29.2%; EGDT INCREASED organ support, LOS and cost
records.why: Completes the triad across 3 health systems; shows over-protocolizing causes harm without benefit
records.note: ProCESS + ARISE + ProMISe is a TEACHING TRIAD — keep together.

records.name: SPICE III
records.q: Early dexmedetomidine vs usual sedation, ventilated adults
records.res: 90-day mortality 29.1 vs 29.1%; more bradycardia and hypotension
records.why: A 'less deliriogenic' sedative does not equal a mortality benefit
records.gl: guidelines have not adopted a mortality-based change
records.note: Metadata cross-referenced via Crossref/Semantic Scholar; NCBI efetch returned empty for this ID.

records.name: SHIFT
records.q: Ivabradine vs placebo, HFrEF in sinus rhythm with HR ≥70
records.res: CV death or HF hosp 24 vs 29%, HR 0.82
records.why: Pure heart-rate reduction independent of beta-blockade improves outcomes

records.name: MADIT-II
records.q: Prophylactic ICD vs medical therapy, prior MI and EF ≤30%
records.res: Mortality 14.2 vs 19.8%, HR 0.69; stopped early
records.why: Primary-prevention ICD on EF alone, no EP testing required

records.name: SCD-HeFT
records.q: Amiodarone vs ICD vs placebo, NYHA II-III HF with EF ≤35%
records.res: ICD ↓ mortality HR 0.77; amiodarone NO benefit (HR 1.06)
records.why: Extends ICD benefit to non-ischemic CM; amiodarone is not a substitute

records.name: PIONEER AF-PCI
records.q: Rivaroxaban-based dual vs warfarin triple therapy after PCI in AF
records.res: Clinically significant bleeding 16.8 / 18.0 vs 26.7%
records.why: With RE-DUAL, established dropping aspirin; set the stage for AUGUSTUS
records.gl: predates AUGUSTUS and current guidance; underpowered for ischemic efficacy

records.name: RE-DUAL PCI
records.q: Dabigatran dual vs warfarin triple therapy after PCI in AF
records.res: Bleeding 15.4 / 20.2 vs 26.9 / 25.7%; noninferior efficacy
records.why: Second pillar of the drop-the-aspirin evidence

records.name: FAME 2
records.q: FFR-guided PCI + medical therapy vs medical therapy alone, stable CAD
records.res: Composite 4.3 vs 12.7%, HR 0.32; stopped early — driven ENTIRELY by urgent revascularization, not death/MI
records.why: Distinct from FAME. The nuance — what actually drove the composite — is the teaching point
records.note: DISTINCT trial from FAME (PMID 19144937). Do not conflate.

records.name: UPLIFT
records.q: Tiotropium vs placebo 4 years, COPD
records.res: Did NOT slow FEV1 decline (primary endpoint) but ↓ exacerbations, ↑ QoL
records.why: Negative primary endpoint with real clinical benefit — why the primary endpoint alone does not decide a drug's value

records.name: NETT
records.q: Lung-volume-reduction surgery vs medical therapy, severe emphysema
records.res: No overall mortality benefit; benefit ONLY in upper-lobe-predominant + low exercise capacity. High-risk subgroup (FEV1 ≤20% + homogeneous emphysema or DLCO ≤20%) had 30-day mortality 16 vs 0%
records.why: Selection is everything; models a real DSMB safety stop
records.gl: incorporated (NETT criteria are a standing contraindication)
records.note: High-risk subgroup reported separately: Fishman NEJM 2001, PMID 11596586.

records.name: CREST
records.q: Carotid stenting vs endarterectomy
records.res: Composite 7.2 vs 6.8% at 4y, no difference; stenting ↑ periprocedural stroke, CEA ↑ periprocedural MI
records.why: The stroke-vs-MI trade-off that drives procedure selection

records.name: RE-SPECT ESUS
records.q: Dabigatran vs aspirin after embolic stroke of undetermined source
records.res: Not superior: 4.1 vs 4.8%/yr, HR 0.85
records.why: With NAVIGATE ESUS, closes the door on empiric anticoagulation for ESUS
records.gl: guidelines retain antiplatelet therapy for ESUS
records.note: DISTINCT from RESPECT (the PFO trial). Confusingly similar names.

records.name: RESPECT (PFO)
records.q: PFO closure vs medical therapy after cryptogenic stroke
records.res: ITT neutral: HR 0.49, p=0.08. The 2017 long-term report (PMID 28902590) reached significance, HR 0.55, p=0.046
records.why: A trial that flipped from neutral to positive with longer follow-up
records.role: evidence reversal (neutral at 2013, positive on long-term follow-up)
records.gl: incorporated via totality with REDUCE/CLOSE (AHA/ASA 2021, AAN 2020)
records.note: This record is the 2013 PRIMARY analysis. Long-term companion: PMID 28902590. DISTINCT from RE-SPECT ESUS.

records.name: CLOSE
records.q: PFO closure vs antiplatelet vs anticoagulation, cryptogenic stroke with HIGH-RISK PFO anatomy
records.res: Recurrent stroke 0% vs 6.0%, p<0.001; ↑ new AF 4.6 vs 0.9%
records.why: Anatomic selection (large shunt or septal aneurysm) produced the largest absolute benefit of any PFO trial

records.name: Look AHEAD
records.q: Intensive lifestyle vs diabetes support/education, T2DM
records.res: STOPPED FOR FUTILITY: CV composite HR 0.95, p=0.51, despite more weight loss and better fitness
records.why: Improving surrogates does not guarantee hard outcome benefit
records.gl: ADA recommends ILI for weight/glycemia, NOT for CV event reduction

records.name: ORIGIN
records.q: Insulin glargine vs standard care, dysglycemia + CV risk
records.res: Neutral: HR 1.02; no cancer excess; more hypoglycemia and weight gain
records.why: Establishes glargine CV/cancer safety, but no CV benefit from early insulin
records.gl: incorporated as safety reassurance (ADA/EASD, FDA CV-safety framework)

records.name: LIFE (geriatrics)
records.q: Structured physical activity vs health education, sedentary adults 70-89
records.res: Major mobility disability 30.1 vs 35.5%, HR 0.82, p=0.03
records.why: One of the few POSITIVE geriatric prevention trials with a hard functional outcome
records.note: DISAMBIGUATION: a different trial named LIFE tests losartan vs atenolol in hypertension with LVH (PMID 11937178). This is the geriatrics mobility trial.

records.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
records.note: ARIA-E 24%, 3 treatment-related deaths — teach the safety tradeoff

records.name: LEAP (levodopa PD)
records.note: NAME AMBIGUOUS: distinct from LEAP peanut-allergy trial

records.name: ADAPT (efgartigimod gMG)
records.note: NAME AMBIGUOUS: distinct from ADAPT NSAID Alzheimer prevention trial

records.name: RITUXVAS
records.gl: incorporated (rituximab induction option in renal AAV)

records.name: TULIP-2
records.note: TULIP-1 failed SRI-4; TULIP-2 met BICLA — endpoint-choice teaching case

records.name: focuSSced
records.gl: incorporated for SSc-ILD only (FDA 2021 despite negative skin endpoint)

records.name: CARES
records.gl: incorporated (FDA febuxostat boxed warning 2019; 2020 ACR gout)

records.name: U-EXCEL / U-EXCEED
records.note: One publication reports BOTH U-EXCEL (less-refractory) and U-EXCEED (biologic-failure)

records.name: MOTIVATE (risankizumab CD)
records.note: Crohn induction, biologic-refractory; paired with ADVANCE
